newsitem.title: UK: CLYDE BLOWERS SEES 30 PCT PRE-TAX HIT 1998. [CORRECTED 9:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CLYDE BLOWERS SEES 30 PCT PRE-TAX HIT 1998. [CORRECTED 9:57 GMT]

text.p: UK engineering group Clyde Blowers said on Monday it expected the strength of sterling to reduce sales and pre-tax profits next year.
(Corrects reference to size of profit hit).

"We have revised our sales forecast down by two million stg for next year which again would have had an average pre-tax contribution of 30 percent," the company said in a trading statement. News that next year's sales will be hurt by the considerable strength of sterling comes on top of a similar expected hit this year.

Over the last three months, the company said it had dropped three million pounds worth of turnover which was previously expected to make a contribution of around 30 percent at both the operating and pre-tax level.
But the group said that despite the strength of sterling, it was still expecting growth next year.
"Despite the effect of the exceptional strength of sterling, our fundamental strategy and prospects are not affected with earnings expected to be strong again next year," it said in a statement.
Clyde Blowers has already reorganised its two businesses and merged operations onto one site in a reorganisation which was expected to help the group's competitive advantage in international markets.
